1.3.0.release_notes:
GKM Core 1.3.0 extends `ConceptSet` (`trial use`) so concept sets can carry a type annotation and reference external concepts by IRI instead of only inlining them, and migrates the schema source to the GKM metaschema processor's 0.4.x abstract-class convention.

Changes below are categorized per the GA4GH TASC [Technical Specification Development](https://www.ga4gh.org/document/tasc-technical-specification-development/) policy's Major/Minor/Patch versioning rules, based on the `maturity` of each class touched.

## Minor Version Increment

- Adds an optional `conceptSetType` field to `ConceptSet` (`trial use`), for annotating the kind of concept a set represents
- Adds `iriReference` as an allowed `ConceptSet.concepts` member (`trial use`), alongside `MappableConcept`/`ConceptSet`, so a concept set can reference an external concept by IRI instead of only inlining it ([`e6e5c1a`](https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/commit/e6e5c1aaf11383673113088b835c2bf749c4d41a))

## Patch Version Increment

- Migrates the schema source to the GKM metaschema processor's 0.4.x abstract-class convention (`heritableProperties`/`heritableRequired` → `properties`/`required` + explicit `abstract: true`); generated JSON Schema output is unchanged in meaning
- Completes the `gks` → `gkm` rebrand in remaining README/CI references ([#141](https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/141))
- Adds a negative-example test harness, concrete-class coverage checks, and schema invariant tests
- Fixes a typo in the `date-time` format description (`YYYY:MM::DD` → `YYYY-MM-DD`)
- Several `ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` processor version bumps (0.4.0 → 0.4.8)

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/compare/1.2.0...1.3.0

1.3.0-ballot.2026-09.1.release_notes:
## What's Changed

Version 1.3.0 adds an optional `conceptSetType` to `ConceptSet`, matching the `conceptType` already on `MappableConcept`. It also moves GKM Core to the renamed `ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` processor and its abstract-class convention. `Entity` and `Element` are now declared `abstract: true` and published as standalone, open JSON Schemas, so downstream specifications (VRS, Cat-VRS, VA-Spec) can reference these root classes directly. The concrete classes stay closed to undefined properties, so existing valid 1.2.0 instances still validate.

Changes are categorized per the GA4GH TASC [Technical Specification Development](https://www.ga4gh.org/document/tasc-technical-specification-development/) policy, based on the `maturity` of each class touched. All GKM Core classes are currently at **trial use**.

### Minor Version Increment
* adds the optional `ConceptSet.conceptSetType` property, which names the kind of concept a `ConceptSet` represents. This adds an optional field to a trial-use class. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138

### Patch Version Increment
* adopts the renamed `ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` processor (formerly `ga4gh.gks.metaschema`), pinned to the published `0.4.8` release, and its abstract-class convention. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138
  * `Entity` and `Element` are marked `abstract: true`; `heritableProperties`/`heritableRequired` become `properties`/`required`.
  * `Entity` and `Element` are now emitted as standalone JSON Schema files (`json/Entity`, `json/Element`). They are left open, with no `additionalProperties`/`unevaluatedProperties` closure.
  * concrete classes are closed by the processor. `MappableConcept` now closes with `unevaluatedProperties: false` instead of `additionalProperties: false`; the instances it accepts are unchanged.
* the generated JSON Schema no longer carries `$comment` annotations. They remain in the source YAML and the generated `def/` docs. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138
* fixes the `datetime` description's format string (`YYYY:MM::DD...` → `YYYY-MM-DD...`). The `format: date-time` constraint is unchanged. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138
* adds a negative-example test harness (`examples/invalid/`, `tests/test_invalid_definitions.yaml`), valid examples for the previously untested `ConceptMapping`, `ConceptSet`, and `Extension` classes, and schema-invariant tests that check the abstract-open / concrete-closed convention against the generated JSON. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138
* links the README to the `ga4gh/gks-metaschema` processor repo and documents the valid/invalid example layout. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138
* sets the schema `$id` version token to `1.3.0-ballot.2026-09.1`. By @larrybabb in https://github.com/ga4gh/gkm-core/pull/138

Version 2.1.1 moves VRS to the renamed GKM metaschema processor (`ga4gh.gkm.metaschema`) and its abstract-class convention, and tracks GKM Core 1.3.0. The abstract classes `Variation`, `MolecularVariation`, `SystemicVariation`, `Location`, and `SequenceExpression` are now declared *sealed*: the processor derives each class's closed set of concrete subclasses instead of relying on hand-maintained `oneOf` lists. The derived sets match 2.1.0 exactly, so the instances VRS accepts and their computed identifiers are unchanged. This release also renames the "Concepts" documentation section to "Model", aligns the maturity model page with the GA4GH TASC [Technical Specification Development](https://www.ga4gh.org/document/tasc-technical-specification-development/) policy, and substantially expands the test suite.

## Patch Version Increment

- Adopts the renamed `ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` processor (`0.4.8`) and its abstract-class convention: abstract classes are marked `abstract: true` and left open, while concrete classes stay closed to undefined properties (`additionalProperties`/`unevaluatedProperties: false`), as they already were in 2.1.0, by @larrybabb in #718
- Declares `Variation`, `MolecularVariation`, `SystemicVariation`, `Location`, and `SequenceExpression` `sealed: true`, replacing their hand-written `oneOf` unions with processor-derived ones. The derived unions are identical to 2.1.0's. Properties that previously inlined a `oneOf` over the sequence expression classes (`Allele.state`, `RelativeAllele.baseState`/`mappedState`, `Adjacency.linker`) now reference `SequenceExpression` instead, which resolves to the same three classes, by @larrybabb in #718
- Publishes `Ga4ghIdentifiableObject` as a standalone, open JSON Schema (`json/Ga4ghIdentifiableObject`) by @larrybabb in #718
- Bumps the gkm-core submodule from `1.2.0` to `1.3.0`. VRS classes that inherit from GKM Core's `Entity` (`Ga4ghIdentifiableObject`, `SequenceExpression`, `SequenceOffsetLocation`, `TraversalBlock`) or `Element` (`Expression`) see no property changes, since 1.3.0 only marks those root classes abstract, by @larrybabb in #718

- Renames the "Concepts" documentation section to "Model", generates the imported GKM Core class definitions locally instead of linking them from the submodule, and fixes the maturity model link, by @larrybabb in #718

Also regenerates the stale `validation/json/models.json`, adding the missing fixtures for the draft intronic-position classes, by @larrybabb in #718
- Updates the pre-commit CI job to check out submodules and install the schema-build dependencies, and makes the `update-json-def-files` hook fail on a `make` error, by @larrybabb in #718

The v1.3.0 release of VRS includes two new systemic variation concepts: 

1. the Genotype model for representing all variants present at a given genomic locus
2. the CopyNumberChange model for representing copy number changes from a regional base ploidy

It also includes support for composed sequence expressions, for expressing sequences composed of multiple underlying expressions.

1.2.0.release_notes:
# Deprecations

- SimpleInterval and SequenceState are deprecated. They will be removed in VRS 2.0.

# Major Changes

- New classification of variation types.
  - Molecular Variation refers to variation within or of a contiguous molecular
  - Systemic Variation refers to variation in the context of a system, such as a genome, sample, or homologous chromosomes
  - Utility Variation classes provide useful representations for certain technical operations

- New SequenceExpressions subclasses replace SequenceState. Subtypes are:
  - DerivedSequenceExpression, which representations sequence notionally derived from a SequenceLocation
  - RepeatedSequenceExpression, which represents contiguous repeats of a sequence
  - LiteralSequenceExpression, which wraps a Sequence and provides data structure parity with other SequenceExpressions

- CopyNumber, a form of SystemicVariation, represents the copies of a molecule within a genome, and can be used to express concepts such as amplification and copy loss.

- Gene enables reference to an external definition of a gene, particularly for useas a subject of copy number expressions.

- DefiniteRange and IndefiniteRange represent bounded and half-bounded ranges respectively. A new Number type wraps integers so that some attributes may assume values of any of these three types.

For more changes, see the [release notes](https://vrs.ga4gh.org/en/stable/releases/1.2.html)

1.1.1.release_notes:
Version 1.1.1 is a **patch** release that modernizes the Cat-VRS build pipeline and advances its imported dependencies (VRS `2.1.1` and GKM Core `1.3.0`). No change alters which instances validate against a **trial use** class, and there are no additions or removals to the set of Cat-VRS product features.

## Patch changes

The following **product features** at **trial use** maturity were modified without changing which instances validate:

- `Constraint`: the abstract base is now declared `sealed`. The metaschema processor renders it as a closed union of its concrete subtypes with a `type` discriminator (matching the VRS abstract-class convention). The derived union is the same seven concrete subtypes that 1.1.0 listed by hand, and every subtype already required `type`. `CategoricalVariant.constraints` now references `Constraint` directly, which resolves to the same set.
- Canonical Allele (and the **draft** Categorical CNV) recipe now declares `unevaluatedProperties: false`. Both recipes already inherited closure from `CategoricalVariant`, so the set of valid instances is unchanged.

## Dependencies

- The Cat-VRS schema identifier (`$id`) is now `https://w3id.org/ga4gh/schema/cat-vrs/1.1.1/...`.
- Imported schemas were advanced to VRS `2.1.1` and GKM Core `1.3.0`. The only data-model changes in GKM Core 1.3.0 — a new optional `ConceptSet.conceptSetType` field and `iriReference` as a new allowed `ConceptSet.concepts` member — do not reach Cat-VRS: Cat-VRS uses `MappableConcept`, which 1.3.0 leaves unchanged, but not `ConceptSet`.

## Supporting changes

The following **supporting** changes were made to Cat-VRS that do not impact the Cat-VRS data model:

- Adopted the modernized GKM metaschema processor (`ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` 0.4.8), with which the source YAMLs are compiled (`source2classes`/`source2splitjs`/`y2t`). Cross-schema references in the recipe definitions now use explicit `$refCurie` (e.g. `cat-vrs:CategoricalVariant`), as required by the stricter 0.4.x processor.
- Cat-VRS now generates and owns the documentation definitions for its imported VRS and GKM Core classes locally, rather than depending on the submodule's pre-generated definitions. Imported VRS class pages link to the full definition in the latest [VRS specification](https://vrs.ga4gh.org/en/latest/).
- Renamed the "Data Model" documentation section to "Model" (consistent with VRS) and consolidated the Constraint documentation onto a single index page.
- The pre-commit CI job now checks out submodules, matching the local hook, so schema regeneration is verified in CI.

# Cat-VRS 1.0.0 Official Release

We are excited to announce the first official release of Cat-VRS, providing a robust foundation for categorical variation representation within the GA4GH GKS ecosystem.

## Major Features

- **Support for Categorical Variation**: Comprehensive modeling of categorical variation, including support for hyperintensional set objects and new requirements for `CategoricalVariation` naming.
- **Expanded and Improved Documentation**: Full decision record, product roadmap, and extensive examples have been integrated into the documentation, including specification examples for complex variants like BRAF V600 and TP-53 CNLoss.
- **Example Expansion**: Significantly expanded set of examples to aid implementers, including canonical alleles, categorical CNVs, protein sequence consequences, and described variants.
- **Improved Specification and Comments**: Updated comments and annotations throughout the code and specification to clarify intent and enhance readability.
- **Infrastructure and Quality**: Updates to support VRS 2.0, improved internal and external hyperlinking, and enhancements to citation formats and design documentation.

## Get Started

For comprehensive documentation, examples, and the product roadmap, please visit our [ReadTheDocs](https://cat-vrs.ga4gh.org/) site.

Thank you to all contributors for making this initial release possible!

Congruent representations of an Allele often exist across different genome assemblies and associated cDNA transcript representations.

CategoricalCnv.description: A categorical variation domain is defined first by a sequence derived from a canonical [Location ](https://vrs.ga4gh.org/en/2.0/terms_and_model.html#Location) , which is representative of  a collection of congruent Locations. The change or count of this sequence is also described, either by a numeric value (e.g. "3 or more copies") or categorical representation (e.g. "high-level gain").  Categorical CNVs may optionally be defined by rules specifying the location match characteristics for  member CNVs.

CategoricalVariation.description: A representation of a categorically-defined domain for variation, in which individual  contextual variation instances may be members of the domain.

DescribedVariation.description: Some categorical variation concepts are supported by custom nomenclatures or text-descriptive representations for which a categorical variation model does not exist. DescribedVariation is a class that adds requirements and contextual semantics to the `label` and `description` fields to indicate how a categorical variation concept should be evaluated for matching variants.

NumberChange.description: A quantitative assessment of a unit within a system (e.g. genome, cell, etc.) relative to a baseline quantity.

NumberCount.description: The absolute count of a discrete assayable unit (e.g. chromosome, gene, or sequence).

ProteinSequenceConsequence.description: A change that occurs in a protein sequence as a result of genomic changes. Due to the degenerate nature of the genetic code, there are often several genomic changes that can cause a protein sequence consequence. The protein sequence consequence, like a CanonicalAllele, is defined by an `Allele <https://vrs.ga4gh.org/en/2.0/terms_and_model.html#variation>` that is representative of a collection of congruent Protein Alleles that share the same altered codon(s).

QuantityVariance.description: The Quantity Variance class captures one axis of variation in the generalized model of categorical variation.  It is used to model quantitative measure changes in a given biological level of variation.

Agent.description: An autonomous actor (person, organization, or software agent) that bears some form of responsibility for an activity taking place, for the existence of an entity, or for another agent's activity.

CohortAlleleFrequencyStudyResult.description: A StudyResult that reports measures related to the frequency of an Allele in a cohort

ComputationalVariantFunctionalImpactAnal.description: An AnalysisResult that reports the output of a single in silico tool's analysis of a variant's functional impact, including any numeric score(s) and optional categorical interpretation.

Condition.description: A specialization of MappableConcept representing a single condition (disease, phenotype, or trait). Allowed conceptType values include: Condition, Phenotype, Disease, Trait, Absent.

ConditionSet.description: A specialization of ConceptSet representing a set of conditions (diseases, phenotypes, traits) that occur together or are related, depending on the membership operator. Concepts are restricted to Condition and ConditionSet members.

Contribution.description: An action taken by an agent in contributing to the creation, modification, assessment, or deprecation of a particular entity (e.g. a Statement, DataSet, Publication, etc.)

DataItem.description: An Information Entity representing an individual piece of data, generated or acquired through methods which reliably produce truthful information about something.

DataSet.description: A collection of related data items or records that are organized together in a common format or structure, to enable their computational manipulation as a unit.

Document.description: A collection of information, usually in a text-based or graphic human-readable form, intended to be read and understood together as a whole.

EvidenceLine.description: An independent, evidence-based argument that may support or refute the validity of a specific Proposition. The strength and direction of this argument is based on an interpretation of one or more pieces of information as evidence for or against the target Proposition.

ExperimentalVariantFunctionalImpactPropo.description: A Proposition describing the impact of a variant on the function sequence feature (typically a gene or gene product).

ExperimentalVariantFunctionalImpactStudy.description: A StudyResult that reports a functional impact score from a variant functional assay or study.

GeneDiseaseValidityProposition.description: A proposition that variants affecting a particular Gene are valid for evaluation as causal for some Condition using appropriate variant classification criteria, given a specific mode of inheritance.

GeneticContextVariantProposition.description: A proposition used to describe knowledge about a variant that includes or depends on its genetic context - e.g. the allelic origin of the variant, or its relationship to a specific gene.

InformationEntity.description: An abstract (non-physical) entity that represents 'information content' carried by physical or digital information artifacts such as books, web pages, data sets, or images.

Method.description: A set of instructions that specify how to achieve some objective.

Proposition.description: An abstract entity representing a possible fact that may be true or false. As abstract entities, Propositions capture a 'sharable' piece of meaning whose identify and existence is independent of space and time, or whether it is ever asserted to be true by some agent.

Statement.description: A claim of purported truth as made by a particular agent, on a particular occasion. Statements may be used to put forth a possible fact (i.e. a 'Proposition') as true or false, or to provide a more nuanced assessment of the level of confidence or evidence supporting a particular Proposition.

StudyGroup.description: A collection of individuals or specimens from the same taxonomic class, selected for analysis in a scientific study based on their exhibiting one or more common characteristics  (e.g. species, race, age, gender, disease state, income). StudyResult.description: A collection of data items from a single study that pertain to a particular subject or experimental unit in the study, along with optional provenance information describing how these data items were generated.

SubjectVariantProposition.description: A Proposition that has a variant as the subject.

Therapy.description: A specialization of MappableConcept representing an individual therapy (drug, procedure, behavioral intervention, etc.). Allowed conceptType values include: Therapy, Absent, Drug, Procedure, Behavioral Intervention.

TherapyGroup.description: A specialization of ConceptSet representing a group of two or more therapies that are applied in combination to a single patient/subject, or applied individually to a different subset of participants in a research study. TumorVariantFrequencyStudyResult.description: A Study Result that reports measures related to the frequency of a variant in a particular tumor type.

VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition.description: A Proposition describing the clinical significance of a variant with respect to a condition.

VariantDiagnosticProposition.description: A Proposition about whether a variant is associated with a disease (a diagnostic inclusion criterion), or absence of a disease (diagnostic exclusion criterion).

VariantMolecularConsequenceProposition.description: A Proposition describing a predicted molecular consequence of a variant on transcript and protein molecules - typically reporting the type of sequence feature affected (e.g. 'intron variant', 'splice-site variant'), or an impact on the processing of the molecule along the path from gene to transcript to polypeptide (e.g. 'missense variant', 'frameshift variant'). VariantOncogenicityProposition.description: A proposition describing the role of a variant in causing a tumor type.

VariantPathogenicityProposition.description: A proposition describing the role of a variant in causing a heritable condition.

VariantPrognosticProposition.description: A Proposition about whether a variant is associated with an improved or worse outcome for a disease.

VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition.description: A Proposition about the role of a variant in modulating the response of a neoplasm to drug administration or other therapeutic procedures.

VariantClinicalSignificanceStatement.description: A statement reporting a conclusion from a single study about the clinical significance of a variant with respect to a condition, based on interpretation of the study's results.

VariantPathogenicityEvidenceLine.description: An Evidence Line that describes how a specific type of information was interpreted as evidence for or against a variant's pathogenicity. VariantPathogenicityStatement.description: A Statement describing the role of a variant in causing an inherited condition.

VariantOncogenicityEvidenceLine.description: An Evidence Line that describes how evidence for a variant was interpreted to determine if a specific CCV 2022 criterion code is met, and the strength that evidence this provides for or against the variant's oncogenicity. An Evidence Line that describes how a specific type of information was interpreted as evidence for or against a variant's oncogenicity. 1.1.0.release_notes:
This release adds a `hasEvidence` attribute to `Statement`, for evidence that is associated with a Statement without saying how it supports or disputes the proposition. The dedicated `EvidenceLine` class (referenced via `hasEvidenceLines`, as in 1.0) remains the way to represent how evidence was weighed, as a nested, scored, directional argument. It also reworks how `Proposition`/`StudyResult` subclasses declare their `subject`/`predicate`/`object`/`focus` attributes, so they inherit under their canonical names instead of being renamed per subclass. It restructures the domain entities around GKM Core's `MappableConcept`/`ConceptSet`: `Therapeutic` is renamed `Therapy`, and single concepts and sets are now separate classes. It also renames the abstract `ClinicalVariantProposition` class. The latter three are backwards-incompatible changes to *trial use* classes; the `hasEvidence` addition is not. The release also adds several new *draft* classes and substantially revises the *draft* community profiles. Finally, it modernizes the schema-generation pipeline and refreshes the imported dependencies to Cat-VRS 1.1.1, VRS 2.1.1, and GKM Core 1.3.0.

## Minor Version Increment

Backwards-incompatible changes to previously-released *trial use* product features, and additions/changes to *trial use* or *normative* data classes, per the `gkm-maturity-model` versioning rules:

- renames the abstract `ClinicalVariantProposition` class (*trial use*) to `GeneticContextVariantProposition`, and updates its definition to describe knowledge that depends on a variant's genetic context
- adopts the GKM Core (formerly GKS-Core) 1.2.0 `MappableConcept` and `ConceptSet` changes (both *trial use* in GKM Core). Both classes now inherit `Entity` and require a `type` discriminator field, which is a backwards-incompatible addition of a required field to these previously-released *trial use* classes. This propagates to the VA-Spec *trial use* classes that specialize them: `Condition` and `Therapy` (specializations of `MappableConcept`), and `ConditionSet` and `TherapyGroup` (specializations of `ConceptSet`)
- restructures the *trial use* domain entities. In 1.0, `Condition` and `Therapeutic` were each a union of a single `MappableConcept` or a set. Now:
  - `Condition` and `Therapy` (renamed from `Therapeutic`) are single concepts that specialize `MappableConcept`, with suggested `conceptType` values that default to `Condition`/`Therapy`.
  - the single-or-set union moves to the attributes that use these classes. For example, a proposition's `object` is now `Condition | ConditionSet | iriReference`, as is `VariantTherapeuticResponseProposition` `conditionQualifier`. These attributes already accepted either a single concept or a set in 1.0, through the `Condition`/`Therapeutic` union.
  - `ConditionSet` and `TherapyGroup` now specialize GKM Core's `ConceptSet`. Their required `conditions`/`therapies` arrays are renamed `concepts`, and a member may now also be given as an `iriReference`. A `TherapyGroup` may now contain nested Therapy Groups; a `ConditionSet` could already contain nested Condition Sets as of 1.0.1.
- adopts GKM Core 1.3.0, which adds an optional `conceptSetType` to `ConceptSet`. Because `ConditionSet` and `TherapyGroup` specialize `ConceptSet`, both *trial use* classes now accept this optional field.

### Subject / object / focus model change

**Backwards-incompatible.** VA-Spec 1.0 renamed the abstract triple attributes in each subclass (e.g. `subject` → `subjectVariant`, `object` → `objectCondition`, `focus` → `focusAllele`). The 0.4.x metaschema processor inherits properties by name and does not permit renaming, so the model has been made consistent with that rule:

- The abstract `Proposition` declares `subject`, `predicate`, and `object` (all required); the abstract `StudyResult` declares `focus` (required). Every subclass now **narrows these in place under the same name** rather than renaming them. Affected serialized property names change: `subjectVariant` → `subject`; `objectCondition` / `objectTumorType` / `objectSequenceFeature` / `objectTherapeutic` → `object`; `focusAllele` / `focusVariant` → `focus`. The *draft* propositions added in this release follow the same rule; their `subjectGene` and `objectConsequence` attributes appeared only in 1.1.0 pre-releases, never in a 1.0.x release. All examples and test fixtures were updated accordingly.
- `CohortAlleleFrequencyStudyResult` also renames `focusAlleleCount` → `focusCount`, `locusAlleleCount` → `locusCount`, and `focusAlleleFrequency` → `alleleFrequency`.
- The abstract base classes (`Proposition`, `StudyResult`, `SubjectVariantProposition`) are **open** and no longer carry a closed `oneOf` of their built-in subtypes. Being open means a reference to one of these bases is not restricted to the schema's own subtypes and -- as with any sealed and abstract class -- carries no `additionalProperties: false`, so any object that satisfies the base's required properties validates against it, including subclasses the schema does not itself declare (see the metaschema appendix for how open vs. closed is encoded). Implementers can therefore define and validate **their own** subclasses of `Proposition` and `StudyResult` against these bases. The *draft* `CustomProposition` class, briefly introduced in an earlier 1.1.0 pre-release for the same purpose, is superseded by this and was removed before this release. `Statement` remains concrete and closed, as before.
- allows an `iriReference` as an alternative to an inline object on attributes that reference other, independently-identifiable Information Entities or concepts, so implementers can reference instead of inline them: `Contribution`.contributor, `VariantPathogenicityProposition`.modeOfInheritanceQualifier/ .penetranceQualifier, `Statement`.proposition/ .strength/.classification, `EvidenceLine`.targetProposition/ .strengthOfEvidenceProvided/.evidenceOutcome, `StudyResult`.sourceDataSet, `CohortAlleleFrequencyStudyResult`.cohort, `TumorVariantFrequencyStudyResult` (*draft*).sampleGroup, `DataSet`.license, and `StudyGroup`.characteristics. Attributes that are new in this release follow the same pattern, including `Statement`.quality and the `sourceDataSet` redeclared by the *draft* `ComputationalVariantFunctionalImpactAnalysisResult`.

### Associating evidence with a Statement

`Statement` gains a `hasEvidence` attribute for evidence that is associated with the Statement. It complements the distinct `EvidenceLine` class rather than replacing it: `hasEvidence` gives no indication of how an item supports or disputes the proposition, whereas Evidence Lines (in `hasEvidenceLines`, as in 1.0) carry that information, as direction and strength or score, and are what a classification rests on. The changes in this subsection are additive, so, unlike the changes above, none of them by itself invalidates data that was valid in 1.0:

- `Statement` gains the `hasEvidence` attribute and a *draft* `quality` attribute. `hasEvidence` associates evidence with a Statement without indicating how it supports or disputes the proposition. It is declared immediately before `hasEvidenceLines`, and its items are a `Statement | StudyResult | DataItem | iriReference` (a prior Statement, Study Result, or Data Item); structured, scored, directional arguments are attached separately via `hasEvidenceLines`. For example, in a CIViC oncogenicity assertion the ClinGen/CGC/VICC criteria codes that drive the classification are Evidence Lines, while the associated CIViC evidence items, which are not part of that code system, go in `hasEvidence`.
- `Statement`'s `direction`, `strength`, `score`, and `classification` attributes were already present in 1.0, so a Statement could already report its own assessment.
- `Statement`'s `hasEvidenceLines` still holds `EvidenceLine | iriReference`, as in 1.0: a Statement is **not** itself usable as an Evidence Line, so a nested, scored, directional argument is always a dedicated `EvidenceLine`.
- the `EvidenceLine` class keeps its 1.0 attributes: `targetProposition`, `directionOfEvidenceProvided`, `strengthOfEvidenceProvided`, `scoreOfEvidenceProvided`, `evidenceOutcome`, and `hasEvidenceItems`. `hasEvidenceItems` is widened from `StudyResult | Statement | EvidenceLine | iriReference` to any `InformationEntity | iriReference`, so it also accepts the new `DataItem`. As in 1.0, because an Evidence Line is itself an Information Entity, Evidence Lines nest by listing subordinate Evidence Lines there (there is no separate `hasEvidenceLines` on Evidence Line).
- all examples and test fixtures were updated accordingly.

## Patch Version Increment

New product features at the *draft* maturity level, changes to existing *draft* features, and supporting changes that do not affect data compatibility:

- adds `GeneDiseaseValidityProposition` (*draft*), a new proposition type for gene-disease validity assertions
- adds `VariantMolecularConsequenceProposition` (*draft*), for representing the predicted molecular consequences of a variant
- adds `VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition` (*draft*), for describing the clinical significance of a variant with respect to a condition
- adds `ComputationalVariantFunctionalImpactAnalysisResult` (*draft*), a `StudyResult` (so it requires `focus`) that reports the output of an in silico tool's analysis of a variant's functional impact
- updates the AAC 2017 Aligned Profiles (*draft*) to better reflect the source guidelines
- enforces enum validation in `primaryCodings` across the AAC/ACMG/CCV (*draft*) profiles
- updates the `ConditionSet` VA-Spec version reference
- resolves a typo ("Oncoogenicity" → "Oncogenicity") in the CCV oncogenicity evidence line profile
- fixes typos in the allele origin description
- updates descriptions for the Variant Clinical Significance Statement profile
- updates the VRS and Cat-VRS submodule references (see the GKM Core items under Minor above for the substantive changes pulled in via these bumps)
- adds Quick Start guidance
- adds documentation for the `TumorVariantFrequencyStudyResult` (*draft*) profile to the Study Result profiles page
- adds a README to the Modeling subdirectory
- updates the repository README to include contributing information
- adds a CITATION file
- various documentation fixes and copyright year updates
- adds test examples and fixtures for CIViC oncogenicity assertions and propositions
- adds a pre-commit hook to detect and stage VA-Spec schema updates
- corrects the core model class diagram to show `DataSet` inheriting from `Entity` rather than `InformationEntity`, matching the source schema (closes [\#380](https://github.com/ga4gh/va-spec/issues/380))
- the 0.4.x metaschema processor now emits a JSON Schema for every abstract class (previously only unions were emitted).

### Draft classes and community profiles

Changes to classes at *draft* maturity, including every AAC-2017, ACMG-2015, and CCV-2022 community profile class. Some of these changes are backwards-incompatible, but draft classes carry no compatibility guarantee, so they are patch-level:

- adds a new draft `DataItem` class (an `InformationEntity` subclass wrapping a structured, string, or IRI-reference `value`) as one of the concrete types citable as evidence (via a Statement's `hasEvidence` or an Evidence Line's `hasEvidenceItems`).
- restructures the AAC-2017 profiles. The 1.0 `VariantDiagnosticStudyStatement`, `VariantPrognosticStudyStatement`, and `VariantTherapeuticResponseStudyStatement` classes are replaced by a single top-level `VariantClinicalSignificanceStatement`, which composes `Statement` and constrains its `classification` attribute, and by four new classes that compose the `EvidenceLine` class (using its `directionOfEvidenceProvided`/`strengthOfEvidenceProvided` attributes): `AmpAscoCapEvidenceLine`, `DiagnosticEvidenceLine`, `PrognosticEvidenceLine`, and `TherapeuticEvidenceLine`. Earlier 1.1.0 pre-releases declared the last three as `type: array` (an array of itself-or-`iriReference`) rather than as plain `allOf`-composed objects, so the tier i/ii `hasEvidenceLines` narrowing that referenced them (via a bare `oneOf`, with no `type: array`/`items` wrapper of its own) required the whole `hasEvidenceLines` array to itself match one of these array-typed branches, rather than letting each item independently be one of the three types. That array-wrapping defect never shipped in a 1.0.x release, and is fixed here: the array wrapping lives at the narrowing site, matching `AmpAscoCapEvidenceLine`'s composition pattern.
- `VariantPathogenicityEvidenceLine` and `VariantOncogenicityEvidenceLine` still compose the `EvidenceLine` class and use its `directionOfEvidenceProvided`/ `strengthOfEvidenceProvided`/`evidenceOutcome` attribute names, as in 1.0. Each class's own `methodType` enumeration is redefined. In 1.0 it listed the individual criterion codes (`PVS1`, `PS1`, ... for ACMG-2015; `OVS1`, `OS1`, ... for CCV-2022). It now lists `snake_case` codes for the type of assessment performed (17 for ACMG-2015, 8 for CCV-2022), and new per-`methodType` `if`/`then` constraints restrict the criterion codes that `evidenceOutcome` may report for each one. Earlier 1.1.0 pre-releases used other names for these codes (e.g. ACMG-2015's `"Population Data Assessment"` → `population_data_assessment` and `"De Novo Data Assessment"` → `de_novo_occurrence_assessment`; CCV-2022's `population_frequency` → `population_data_assessment`, `functional_assay` → `functional_data_assessment`, `functional_domain_location` → `functional_domain_assessment`, `amino_acid_or_residue_analogy` → `amino_acid_analogy_assessment`, `somatic_hotspot_recurrence` → `somatic_hotspot_assessment`, `computational_prediction` → `in_silico_impact_assessment`, and `single_genetic_etiology_context` → `single_genetic_etiology_assessment`). The CCV-2022 statement profile is renamed from `VariantOncogenicityStudyStatement` to `VariantOncogenicityStatement`. It and `VariantPathogenicityStatement` constrain the core `Statement` `classification` attribute, as in 1.0.
- both `VariantPathogenicityEvidenceLine` and `VariantOncogenicityEvidenceLine` add `no_criteria_met` as an allowed `evidenceOutcome` code, alongside the existing `{criterion_code}` and `{criterion_code}_not_met` forms. Use it to report that the criteria associated with the evidence line's `methodType` were assessed, but none of them were met. It is accepted both by each class's overall outcome pattern and by every per-`methodType` pattern. **Backwards-incompatible:** both classes now also constrain the *direction* and *strength* that may accompany a negative outcome: when `evidenceOutcome` is `no_criteria_met` or any `{criterion_code}_not_met` code, `directionOfEvidenceProvided` MUST be `neutral` and `strengthOfEvidenceProvided` MUST NOT be present. Previously a not-met outcome could be paired with a `supports`/`disputes` direction and a strength value.
- the 17 ACMG-2015 per-`methodType` conditions on `VariantPathogenicityEvidenceLine` check the correctly-nested `specifiedBy.methodType` (matching the equivalent pattern on `VariantOncogenicityEvidenceLine`). The 1.1.0 pre-releases that introduced these conditions checked a non-existent top-level `methodType` property instead, so none of them could ever be satisfied by a valid instance. That defect never shipped in a 1.0.x release.
- constrains `hasEvidenceLines` in the ACMG-2015 (*draft*) and CCV-2022 (*draft*) statement profiles to the profile's own evidence line class or an `iriReference`. In 1.0 these profiles did not narrow `hasEvidenceLines`, which therefore accepted any `EvidenceLine | iriReference`. The AAC-2017 `VariantClinicalSignificanceStatement` narrows it the same way, to its three evidence line classes or an `iriReference`, for tier i and tier ii classifications.

### Pipeline modernization

Supporting changes to the schema-generation tooling and repository layout that do not, by themselves, change the meaning of VA-Spec data:

- migrates the metaschema processor from `ga4gh.gks.metaschema` (0.3.2) to the renamed `ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` (0.4.8) package (the GKS → GKM "Genomic Knowledge Models" rebrand). The console entrypoints (`source2classes`, `source2splitjs`, `y2t`) are unchanged, so `make all` still drives generation. 0.4.6 tightens `$ref` handling: a `$ref` must be a local `#/$defs/...` reference, so the bare-class-name and full-URL `$ref`s previously used to reach classes in an imported module (`domain-entities`, and the base `va-spec` classes referenced from the community profiles) were converted to `$refCurie: <namespace>:<Class>`. 0.4.7 adds two purely additive generated-docs features: an `allOf`-composed class's def page now carries a **Composes:** line naming the class it composes onto (mirroring the existing **Inherits:**/\*\*Subclasses:\*\* lines for `inherits:`-based classes), and a composed class with `if`/`then` constraints now renders a table summarizing them (e.g. the AAC-2017 tier-based rules on `VariantClinicalSignificanceStatement`). 0.4.8 renames that table from "Conditional Constraints" to **Additional Constraints**, adds italic/bold styling to the property/value cells, and gives `anyOf`/`oneOf` compositions whose only constraint is "at least one of" a plain-language sentence instead of a duplicated placeholder bullet list (see `MappableConcept`, which requires at least one of `name` or `primaryCoding`).
- adopts the 0.4.x source conventions in every VA-Spec module source: abstract classes are marked `abstract: true` (left open by omitting `additionalProperties: false`), concrete classes are closed and drop the explicit `type: object` (the processor injects it), `heritableProperties` / `heritableRequired` become plain `properties` / `required` on abstract bases, and the removed `extends:` key is dropped.
- renames the nested `gks-core` import to `gkm-core` throughout the schema sources, imported `$refCurie` namespaces (`gks.core` → `gkm.core`), and the documentation.
- makes the imported `schema/{cat-vrs,vrs,gkm-core}` directories real folders that symlink only to the imported `*-source.yaml` and `json/` (no `def/`); VA-Spec now generates the imported-class `def/` locally via `y2t` and the docs include those local defs.
- checks out submodules recursively in the pre-commit CI job so `make all` can resolve the imported source symlinks on a fresh checkout.
- reorganizes `schema/va-spec/`: the former `base/` module moves up to the `va-spec/` root (`va-core-source.yaml` is renamed `va-spec-source.yaml`), and the build now produces a single `json/` and `def/` under `va-spec/`. Each community profile writes its own classes into `json/<community>/` and `def/<community>/` subfolders (the base classes' output sits at the `json/` and `def/` root). Base-class namespaces change from `va-spec.base` to `va-spec`; community namespaces (`va-spec.aac-2017` etc.) are unchanged.
- flattens the three community profile sources — `aac-2017/profile-source.yaml`, `acmg-2015/profile-source.yaml`, `ccv-2022/profile-source.yaml` — out of their own subdirectories, into `schema/va-spec/<community>-profile-source.yaml`, alongside `va-spec-source.yaml` and `domain-entities-source.yaml`. This adopts the `gks-metaschema` processor's native **profile sub-namespace** convention (an `XXX-profile-source.yaml` file contributes `XXX` as a sub-namespace of the folder it lives in): outputs land at `json/<community>/` and `def/<community>/`, and each profile class's `$id` is now `.../va-spec/<version>/json/<community>/<Class>` (in 1.0 it was `.../va-spec/<version>/<community>/json/<Class>`), computed natively by the processor. The four per-directory Makefiles/`prune.mk` are replaced by one flat `schema/va-spec/Makefile`/`prune.mk` that builds every source in the folder. A side benefit: cross-reference ("Used in:") lists in the generated docs are computed across every source in a folder together, so base classes now correctly show community profile classes that reference them (previously invisible across the old subdirectory boundaries).
- makes the documentation fully self-contained: `docs/source` no longer references anything outside itself. Generated class defs are synced into `docs/source/def/` (via `tools/sync-docs-def.sh`, wired into the pre-commit hook), and the Maturity Model page and its images are materialized locally rather than included from the vrs submodule.

### Dependency / version refresh

- bumps the `cat-vrs` submodule to `1.1.1`, which pulls in `vrs` `2.1.1` and `gkm-core` `1.3.0`.
- retargets the imported namespace mappings in every VA-Spec source to the new imported `$id` tokens (`cat-vrs/1.1.1`, `vrs/2.1.1`, `gkm-core/1.3.0`).
- sets VA-Spec's own `$id` token to `1.1.0`.

1.1.0-ballot.2026-09.1.release_notes:
## What's Changed

Version 1.1.0 consolidates the core `EvidenceLine` class into `Statement`: a "discrete evidence-based argument" is now a Statement referenced through another Statement's `hasEvidenceLines`. It also has `Proposition`/`StudyResult` subclasses narrow `subject`/`predicate`/`object`/`focus` in place instead of renaming them per subclass. It restructures the domain entities around GKM Core's `MappableConcept`/`ConceptSet` (`Therapeutic` is renamed `Therapy`) and renames the abstract `ClinicalVariantProposition`. The release also adds several *draft* propositions, substantially revises the *draft* AAC-2017, ACMG-2015, and CCV-2022 community profiles, modernizes the schema-generation pipeline, and refreshes the imported dependencies to the 2026-09 ballot line.

Changes are categorized per the GA4GH TASC [Technical Specification Development](https://www.ga4gh.org/document/tasc-technical-specification-development/) policy, based on the `maturity` of each class touched, and compared against the last full release, **1.0.1**. See the [release log](https://va-spec.ga4gh.org/en/1.1.0-ballot.2026-09/releases/1.1.html) for full detail.

### Minor Version Increment
Backwards-incompatible changes and additions to *trial use* classes:
* **Evidence Line consolidated into Statement.** `EvidenceLine` is removed.
  * `Statement` gains `hasEvidenceItems`, and its `hasEvidenceLines` now holds `Statement | iriReference` (was `EvidenceLine | iriReference`).
  * `EvidenceLine`'s attributes move onto `Statement`: `targetProposition` → `proposition`, which is now optional; `directionOfEvidenceProvided` → `direction`; `strengthOfEvidenceProvided` → `strength`; `evidenceOutcome` and Statement's `classification` merge into `outcome`; `qualityOfEvidenceProvided` → `quality`.
* **Subject / object / focus.** `Proposition` declares `subject`/`predicate`/`object` and `StudyResult` declares `focus`, and every subclass narrows them in place: `subjectVariant` → `subject`; `objectCondition`/`objectTumorType`/`objectSequenceFeature`/`objectTherapeutic` → `object`; `focusAllele`/`focusVariant` → `focus`. The abstract `Proposition`, `StudyResult`, and `SubjectVariantProposition` bases are now open, so implementers can define their own subclasses.
* **Domain entities restructured.**
  * `Therapeutic` is renamed `Therapy`.
  * `Condition` and `Therapy` are now single `MappableConcept` specializations, and the single-or-set union moves to where they're used (e.g. `object`: `Condition | ConditionSet | iriReference`).
  * `ConditionSet` and `TherapyGroup` now specialize `ConceptSet`, with `conditions`/`therapies` renamed `concepts`.
* **Adopts GKM Core 1.2.0 `MappableConcept`/`ConceptSet`.** Both now require a `type` discriminator, which propagates to `Condition`, `Therapy`, `ConditionSet`, and `TherapyGroup`.
* **Adopts GKM Core 1.3.0.** `ConditionSet` and `TherapyGroup` now accept the optional `conceptSetType`.
* **Renames** `ClinicalVariantProposition` → `GeneticContextVariantProposition`.
* **Renames** `CohortAlleleFrequencyStudyResult` `focusAlleleCount` → `focusCount`, `locusAlleleCount` → `locusCount`, and `focusAlleleFrequency` → `alleleFrequency`.
* **Allows an `iriReference`** in place of an inline object on attributes that reference independently-identifiable entities. Examples: `Contribution.contributor`, `Statement.proposition`/`.strength`/`.outcome`/`.quality`, `StudyResult.sourceDataSet`, and `VariantPathogenicityProposition`'s qualifiers.

### Patch Version Increment
New *draft* features, changes to *draft* classes, and supporting changes:
* adds `GeneDiseaseValidityProposition`, `VariantMolecularConsequenceProposition`, `VariantClinicalSignificanceProposition`, and `DataItem` (all *draft*).
* revises the *draft* community profiles:
  * AAC-2017: `AmpAscoCapStatement` and its `Diagnostic`/`Prognostic`/`TherapeuticStatement` subclasses.
  * ACMG-2015 and CCV-2022: evidence lines and statements now compose `Statement`; `methodType` codes are normalized to `snake_case`; `no_criteria_met` outcomes are added; the `if`/`then` tier constraints are fixed; and `hasEvidenceLines` accepts IRIs.
* migrates the metaschema processor to `ga4gh.gkm.metaschema` 0.4.8 and its source conventions, and emits a JSON Schema for every abstract class.
* reorganizes `schema/va-spec/` into a flat folder using the processor's profile sub-namespace convention, and makes the docs self-contained.
* refreshes dependencies to the 2026-09 ballot line: Cat-VRS `1.1.1`, VRS `2.1.1`, and GKM Core `1.3.0` (#446).
* various documentation, example, test-fixture, and tooling updates.

# VA-Spec 1.0.0 Official Release

The GA4GH Variant Annotation Specification (VA-SPEC) 1.0.0 is now released! This milestone establishes a robust standard for representing variant annotation data in genomic research and clinical applications.

## Major Changes Over Ballot Cycle

- **Finalized Variant Annotation Model**: Comprehensive schema for representing variant annotation, including support for study results, source datasets, and profile metadata.
- **Documentation and ReadMe Updates**: Documentation has been thoroughly updated for v1, including class/attribute descriptions and improved onboarding information.
- **Schema and Metadata Enhancements**:
  - Type of the `pmid` field changed from integer to string for broader compatibility.
  - All `profile-source.yaml` files merged into a single unified source.
  - Refined metadata for improved clarity and consistency.
- **Release Preparation and Housekeeping**:
  - Merged all ballot updates for the 2025-03 cycle.
  - Streamlined documentation build process and fixed ReadTheDocs branch handling.

## Getting Started

For comprehensive documentation and schema details, please visit the [ReadTheDocs](https://va-spec.ga4gh.org/) site.

---

Thanks to all contributors for their hard work on this foundational release!
